title: Heinrich Böll Foundation: International Graduate Scholarship
summary: Support for international applicants entering a first Master's programme in Germany, with priority for applicants from DAC countries who are still living abroad.

degree_levels.notes: The September 2026 checklist permits international Master's applicants and the main phase of Diplom/State Examination after the intermediate examination. Apply before that study phase starts.

subject_areas.notes: The application page explicitly accepts all disciplines.

values: State or state-recognised university in Germany
institutions.notes: Check the applicable EU/non-EU funding route and any permitted periods abroad.

nationality.notes: The English application page names EU and DAC countries; the German study page and checklists distinguish EU/non-EU routes and DAC priority. These are not an exhaustive country whitelist. Confirm the current route with the provider.

residence.notes: Not specified in the collected source.

mandatory.text: For the Master's route, complete the first degree abroad and apply before starting the programme. For Diplom/State Examination, apply before the main study phase after the intermediate examination.
The current English Master's section requires full-time study at a state-recognised university; check the route-specific rules in the September 2026 checklist.
The Master's programme must have a standard duration of at least four semesters.
Submit a complete online application through the foundation's portal.
German B2 or DSH 1 proof is required, preferably with the application and at the latest by selection stage III, under the September 2026 checklist.
Strong academic performance, civic engagement, political interest and convincing reasons for applying are selection criteria.

preferences.text: Priority to applicants from DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany.

exceptions.text: Admission or enrolment confirmation may be submitted later, but no later than the third-stage interview, subject to the foundation's instructions.

funding.description: October 2026 overview: the non-EU AA study route lists EUR 992/month plus conditional allowances. The EU/Bildungsinlaender BMFTR study route is income-dependent, up to EUR 855 plus a EUR 300 monthly study-cost allowance. A single universal award amount would be misleading; income and additional support rules vary by route.
funding.duration: Standard study period, with a possible one-semester extension according to the September 2026 checklist.

application_rounds.notes: The German page and September 2026 checklist explicitly describe the international Master's route, but the English landing page still says only first-cycle applications from March 2027. Confirm this conflict before relying on the round.

required_documents.text: Scholarship application form with CV, study motivation and civic engagement
University entrance qualification and translations where needed
Transcript if study has begun; first-degree certificate or confirmation all qualifying examinations were passed for Master's applications
Enrolment/admission confirmation, at the latest by stage III under the stated exception
Written German B2 or DSH 1 proof, at the latest by stage III
Third-party civic-engagement reference on the foundation form
Academic expert reference on the foundation form; it must come from a different person than the civic reference
Other route-specific evidence requested by the checklist or portal

steps.text: Check the formal requirements and deadline.
Compile the checklist documents and expert reports.
Register when the portal opens, complete the application and upload all documents.
